questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours and Pipe B can fill the same tank in 4 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Together: 1/6 + 1/4 = 2/12 + 3/12 = 5/12 per hour. Time = 12/5 hours = 2.4 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes. **Short Trick:** Combined = (6×4)/(6+4) = 24/10 = 2.4 hours.

questions.stem: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, the tank gets filled in 15 hours instead. In how many hours will the leak alone empty a full tank?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Fill rate without leak = 1/10. Effective fill rate with leak = 1/15. Leak rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30 per hour. The leak alone will empty the full tank in 30 hours.

questions.stem: A pipe fills half a tank in 5 hours. How long will it take to fill the complete tank?
questions.explanation: D is correct. If half the tank fills in 5 hours, the full tank fills in 5 × 2 = 10 hours. The pipe fills at a constant rate of 1/10 per hour (since 10 hours for a full tank → 5 hours for half).

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours. Pipe B fills the same tank in 12 hours. Pipe A is opened alone for 2 hours, then Pipe B is also opened. How many more hours after B opens will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In 2 hours, A fills 2/8 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. A+B together: 1/8+1/12 = 3/24+2/24 = 5/24 per hour. Time to fill 3/4 = (3/4)÷(5/24) = (3/4)×(24/5) = 18/5 = 3.6 hours = 3 hours 36 minutes.

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. All three are opened simultaneously. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Combined rate = 1/6+1/8+1/12 = 4/24+3/24+2/24 = 9/24 = 3/8 per hour. Time = 8/3 hours = 2 hours 40 minutes. Check: 8/3 × 3/8 = 1 ✓.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours, Pipe B fills it in 15 hours, and Pipe C (a drain) empties it in 10 hours. If all three are opened simultaneously, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Net rate = 1/12 + 1/15 − 1/10. LCM(12,15,10) = 60. Rate = 5/60 + 4/60 − 6/60 = 3/60 = 1/20 per hour. Tank fills in 20 hours.

questions.stem: Two pipes together fill a tank in 6 hours. One of the pipes alone takes 10 hours. How many hours does the other pipe take alone?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Together rate = 1/6. Pipe 1 rate = 1/10. Pipe 2 rate = 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Pipe 2 alone takes 15 hours. **Short Trick:** Other = (T×A)/(A−T) = (6×10)/(10−6) = 60/4 = 15 hours.

questions.stem: A pipe can fill a tank alone in 5 hours. With a leak, the full tank empties in how many hours if with the leak, filling takes 6 hours?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Without leak: 1/5 per hour. With leak: 1/6 per hour. Leak rate = 1/5 − 1/6 = 6/30 − 5/30 = 1/30 per hour. A full tank empties via the leak alone in 30 hours.

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B fill a tank alternately — first A for one hour, then B for one hour, and so on. A fills the tank in 3 hours alone and B fills it in 6 hours alone. Starting with A, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Per 2-hour cycle (A 1 hr + B 1 hr): A fills 1/3, B fills 1/6. Together: 1/3+1/6 = 1/2 per 2 hours. After 2 hours: 1/2 filled. After 4 hours: 1/2+1/2 = 1 = full. Check if tank fills mid-cycle: after hour 3 (A's second turn): 1/2+1/3=5/6. After hour 4 (B's second turn): 5/6+1/6=1. Full at exactly 4 hours ✓.

questions.stem: 8 identical pipes working together can fill a tank in 6 hours. After 3 hours of all 8 pipes running, 2 pipes are closed. How many more hours will the remaining pipes take to fill the rest of the tank?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total work = 8×6 = 48 pipe-hours. First 3 hours with 8 pipes: 3×8 = 24 pipe-hours done. Remaining = 48−24 = 24 pipe-hours. After closing 2 pipes: 6 pipes left. Time = 24÷6 = 4 more hours.
